methods.label: Equal areas and the Pythagorean theorem
methods.explanation:
The equal areas let us find the missing leg \(CE\) before finding the hypotenuse \(DE\).

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_8_Q14_question_fig1.svg)

Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so \(DC=AB=5\). The rectangle has area \(6\cdot5=30\). Since triangle \(DCE\) has the same area and its legs \(DC\) and \(CE\) are perpendicular,
\[
\frac{5\cdot CE}{2}=30,
\qquad CE=12.
\]
The right angle is at \(C\), so \(DE\) is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
DE^2=5^2+12^2=25+144=169.
\]
A length is positive, so \(DE=13\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary area formulas and the Pythagorean theorem, both appropriate for AMC 8.
